confirmed.title: The notifications inbox labels every decision packet a "completion report"
confirmed.what_user_sees: On /notifications, the "Waiting on you" panel renders one row per open decision. A packet the operator opened to ask a scoping question shows the title "Decision needed: Which scope should we take?" (written at app/server/tasks/operator-actions.server.ts:855) with a pill beside it reading "completion report". Opening the same task shows that packet's own pill reading "Decision required" (the string written at operator-actions.server.ts:786). ntfPill returns `label: "completion report"` for EVERY non-blocked packet — it is the fall-through branch, not a type test.
confirmed.why_wrong: "Completion report" is a specific, load-bearing concept elsewhere in the product: it is the timeline event type label (app/features/task-detail/event-meta.ts:21 `completion: … label: "Completion report"`) and it is what the Review queue says lands at the acceptance boundary ("Completion reports land here when a task reaches the boundary", review-page.tsx:181). Using it as the generic name for any input-type packet means the one word points at two different things, and it actively mis-triages: a supervisor scanning the inbox reads "completion report" and expects something to accept, when the operator is actually asking a question it cannot proceed without. The row contradicts its own title one line to its left.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make ntfPill name the packet, not guess at it. `if (n.kind === "approval") return { kind: "info", label: "approval" }; if (n.ptype === "blocked") return { kind: "blocked", label: "blocked decision" }; return { kind: "input", label: "decision required" };` — matching the `kind` string the packet itself carries (operator-actions.server.ts:786 writes "Blocked decision" | "Decision required"). Better still, thread the packet's stored `kind` string through the notification row so the two surfaces cannot drift again.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: `ntfPill` labels the pill by fall-through rather than by packet type, so EVERY non-blocked ("input") packet row on /notifications reads "completion report" — correct only for the acceptance-boundary shape (`accept_completion` is a real PACKET_OPTION_KIND, app/schemas/task-file.schema.ts:69) and wrong for every other input packet the operator opens (scoping question, redirect, edit_goal, archive_task, retry_other_backend). Do not claim the label is never right; claim it is applied unconditionally. The concrete contradiction to lead with is intra-row and cross-surface: the row's own title is always "Decision needed: …" (operator-actions.server.ts:855) and the same packet is pilled "Decision required" on the task detail (operator-actions.server.ts:786 → decision-packet.tsx:163) and in the review queue row sub. One compounding detail worth including: the sibling fall-through in `ntfMeta` (notification-meta.ts:24-28) also gives every non-blocked packet the `check` icon and the `act-completion` color, so the completion framing is visual as well as verbal — a question renders with a completion checkmark.

Two refinements to the claim as written. (1) It understates the scope: this is not an occasional mismatch but a total one — since `operatorOpenPacket` is the sole writer of packet notifications and always titles them "Decision needed: X" / "Blocked — decision needed: X", there is no reachable input-packet row whose title is a completion report, so the "completion report" pill is wrong on 100% of real rows, including genuine completion packets (whose row still reads "Decision needed:"). (2) The claim cites operator-actions.server.ts:855 for the title; the notify block spans 848-857 with the title expression at 852-855 and the packet's own `kind` string at 786 — both correct, just noting the notify call is the whole block.

confirmed.title: The Review queue names a capability label that was deliberately retired, then tells you to go find it on Policy
confirmed.what_user_sees: On an Autonomous-preset project, the Review queue's acceptance note reads: "…runs at full autonomy with **Completion for human acceptance** set to *Direct*…", and the header chip's tooltip (review-page.tsx:151) says the same plus "See Policy." Following that instruction to Policy → Workflow rules, the equivalent note reads "…with **Accept completion into Done** set to *Direct*…" (policy-page.tsx:515), and the operator profile on the Agents page lists the grant as "Accept completion into Done". No control anywhere in the app is called "Completion for human acceptance".
confirmed.why_wrong: The label was renamed on purpose and the reason is recorded at app/shared/capabilities.ts:50-52: `cap("completion-for-acceptance", "Accept completion into Done", …)` with the comment "the old label ('Completion for human acceptance') read as a guarantee it does not make." The Review queue is the only surface still rendering the retired string — and it is the surface that sends the reader to Policy to verify it, so the user arrives looking for a setting under a name that no longer exists. The code comment at review-page.tsx:187-189 even asserts "wording tracks the Policy note (policy-page.tsx)", which is now false. app/features/review/review-page.test.tsx:269 pins the stale string, so the drift is currently protected by a test.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Replace both occurrences (review-page.tsx:151 and :197) with "Accept completion into Done", and update review-page.test.tsx:269. Ideally import the label from `UNIFIED_CAP_CATALOG` by id (`completion-for-acceptance`) in both review-page.tsx and policy-page.tsx so the rendered name can only come from the catalog.
corrections: Narrower accurate framing: the defect is a label mismatch between two surfaces, not a false statement about behavior — the Review queue's description of the exception (full autonomy + explicit Direct grant, still refuses failing validation, always audited) matches Policy and matches enforcement. Two precision notes: the retired string also appears in design/html-app/app/data.js:562, but that is the static design prototype rather than shipped app copy, so "the Review queue is the only surface still rendering it" holds for the product; and the test at app/features/review/review-page.test.tsx:269 asserts `note).toContain("Completion for human acceptance")`, so fixing the copy requires updating that assertion — there is no lint rule enforcing capability-label consistency across surfaces, which is why the rename missed this file.

One imprecision in the claim's framing worth carrying into the writeup: the Autonomous preset ALONE does not produce this state. `completion-for-acceptance` is seeded at `recommend` with `promotable: false` (app/shared/capabilities.ts:52), so raising autonomy never silently promotes it — an admin must set the grant to Direct explicitly in the operator profile editor. The state therefore requires full autonomy PLUS the explicit Direct grant (resolveAcceptanceAuthority checks all three: deployed, autonomy === "full", gate() === "direct"). That does not weaken the finding — the combination is the documented Q1 path and is reachable entirely through supported admin UI — but the finding should say "a full-autonomy project whose operator holds the explicit Direct grant" rather than "an Autonomous-preset project". Fix scope is three edits: review-page.tsx:151 and :197 to "Accept completion into Done", plus the now-stale assertion at review-page.test.tsx:269.

Also worth noting for the fix: `run_reviewer: "Run reviewer"` (:56) is consistent with its role name, which makes "Run specialist" the single odd chip in the map — the minimal fix is KIND_LABEL.run_specialist -> "Run delivering agent", and no existing test asserts the old string, so nothing needs updating alongside it.

confirmed.title: The engagements cell can be headed "Supporting agents" while every control inside it says "reviewer"
confirmed.what_user_sees: `reviewingAgentsLabel` flips the Execution profile cell heading to "Supporting agents" when every engaged agent is known to hold no verdict grant (execution-profile.tsx:56-66). The controls inside that same cell are unchanged: the add button reads "Engage reviewer" (:388), its menu is aria-labelled "Engage a reviewer" with the empty state "All deployed agents are already reviewing." (:395), each row's release button is titled "Release reviewer" with aria-label "Release {role} reviewer" (:762-763), and on a closed task the cell reads "Task closed — no new reviewer engagements." (:362).
confirmed.why_wrong: The heading was introduced (UC-13, comment at :602-609) precisely so a task with only supporting engagements would stop reading as if it had reviewers holding the acceptance gate — but the fix stopped at the heading. A user who has deliberately engaged non-verdict agents sees a section that says these are supporting agents and then offers only reviewer verbs, which re-asserts exactly the gating relationship the heading just denied. It also makes the menu's own honest tooltip ("has no verdict grant — it can review and comment, but its opinion does not gate acceptance", :411) read as a contradiction of the button that opened it.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Derive the control copy from the same predicate as the heading: when `reviewingAgentsLabel` returns "Supporting agents", render "Engage agent" / "Release agent" / "Task closed — no new engagements" / "All deployed agents are already engaged."; keep the reviewer wording for the "Reviewing agents" case. Pass the resolved label (or a boolean) into `ReviewerControl` rather than computing it twice.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: "Supporting agents" (execution-profile.tsx:56-65, rendered at :724) is the only place in the entire product that uses that term — every other word in the same cell and every related surface elsewhere (rec chips "Reviewer"/"Run reviewer", the run-retry tooltip, the assign/run/remove-reviewer actions, the RBAC role) calls these engagements reviewers. The user-visible failure is therefore a dead-end vocabulary, not a contradicted gate: a user who clicked "Engage reviewer" and picked an agent the menu described as able to "review and comment" watches the section heading rename itself to a word that appears nowhere else, with no explanation of what changed and no way to map "Supporting agents" back to the "Engage reviewer" control, the "Release reviewer" button, or the "Reviewer" recommendation chip on the same page. The coherent fix is to make the label and the surrounding verbs speak one vocabulary (either both "reviewer" with the gating distinction carried by the existing verdict badge/tooltip, or both the engagement vocabulary), not to argue the controls assert gating — they do not.

Two refinements. (1) Severity framing: this is not an exotic combination — because the verdict grant is off by default, "Supporting agents" over reviewer-named controls is what a fresh self-hosted setup shows the first time anyone engages a second agent. (2) The sharpest string is not the add button but the menu empty state at execution-profile.tsx:395, "All deployed agents are already reviewing.": on a small project (one delivering agent, one verdict-less agent engaged) the cell simultaneously says the engagements are supporting, not reviewing, and that all deployed agents are already reviewing — a flat contradiction inside one cell. The add button (:388), release control (:762-763) and closed-task line (:362) are vocabulary drift rather than false statements, since they name the engagement type rather than claiming anyone holds the acceptance gate. It does not block the user; nothing here is a dead end and the menu still discloses which agents gate acceptance via the " · gates acceptance" suffix (:423).

confirmed.title: The agent-log run picker calls interrupted and queued runs "idle", four lines of markup from the pill that calls them "interrupted · by Arda" and "queued"
confirmed.what_user_sees: On a task with several runs, the escalation engineer opens the Agent logs panel and drops the run picker. A run a teammate interrupted is listed as "idle" with a neutral dot; a run waiting for a runtime slot is also listed as "idle". Selecting either one, the pill immediately below in the same panel reads "interrupted · by Arda" (or "queued") and the footer reads "interrupted by Arda — the thread stays resumable" (or "queued — waiting for a runtime slot; output appears once it starts", :447-453). Same run, same panel, one word apart: idle vs interrupted. A run that failed because the backend was out of quota is listed as "continuity error" in the picker while the footer says "Codex was unavailable (quota / rate limit)".
confirmed.why_wrong: Ruling 11 makes `queued|running|finished|error|interrupted` the run lifecycle, and `runs-helpers.ts:24-36` is the module written to render it — its own docstring says "the pill copy for interrupted is handled by the UI reading `lifecycle`". The picker bypasses it and reads `RUN_STATE[r.state]`, the four-value RENDER projection, in which `renderStateOf` collapses both `queued` and `interrupted` to `"idle"` (run-projection.server.ts:132-134). UI-57 already ruled on this exact confusion for the footer — "a QUEUED run is not an idle thread" — and UI-38 already ruled that a backend-unavailable failure must not be called a continuity error; neither fix reached the picker, which is the surface a user reads FIRST to choose which run to inspect.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the picker option (runs-panels.tsx:130-133) call `runStatePill(r)` instead of `RUN_STATE[r.state]`, so the list, the pill and the footer read one vocabulary. Drive the dot class off the same result rather than the raw render state.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: in the Agent logs panel the run picker's dropdown options label a run by its coarse render state (runs-panels.tsx:130-133, RUN_STATE[r.state]) instead of its lifecycle, so an entry whose latest run was interrupted — or is still queued — reads "idle" while the pill and footer in the same panel, four lines below, read "interrupted · by <name>" / "queued — waiting for a runtime slot". Two corrections to the framing: (1) the picker lists ONE ENTRY PER AGENT, not per run (run-projection.server.ts:264-296 groups by groupKeyOf and shows pickRepresentative's state), so it is not a list of several runs each mislabeled — it is the operator/specialist/reviewer entries carrying their representative run's state; the durable, easily reproduced case is an interrupted specialist, while a queued entry is usually a short window. (2) The "continuity error" half is weaker than stated: the picker shows the generic error label while the footer elaborates "Codex was unavailable (quota / rate limit)" — vocabulary leakage of the phrase UI-38 rejected, not a flat same-word contradiction. The fix is one line: have the picker option use runStatePill(r) (runs-helpers.ts:28-37), the module already written for ruling 11.

Two scope corrections to the claim as titled.

1. The queued half is technically reachable but much weaker than the interrupted half. `startRun` inserts `state: "queued"` and the adapter flips it to running immediately after (`run-service.server.ts:374`, :806), so "queued" is a sub-second window a loader would have to catch; and `pickRepresentative` prefers a running row, so a queued resume of an agent that still has a live run never becomes the picker entry. Lead the finding on the interrupted case, which is a durable terminal state.

2. The "continuity error" vs "Codex was unavailable (quota / rate limit)" sentence is misattributed to the picker. `runStatePill` returns `RUN_STATE.error` for `state: "error"`, so the PILL says "continuity error" too — picker and pill agree there. The mismatch is pill-vs-footer (`runs-panels.tsx:458-461`), it exists independently of the picker, and the fixed "continuity error" pill label is what ruling 11 mapped. Either drop that sentence or file it separately; folding it in makes the finding look like it was written from the diff rather than the screen.

Accurate one-line statement of the defect: `AgentPicker` (runs-panels.tsx:132) reads `RUN_STATE[r.state]` instead of `runStatePill(r)`, so it is the only surface in the app that renders an interrupted run's state without ruling 11's lifecycle mapping — four lines of markup from the pill that applies it.

confirmed.title: Switching the board from Board to List drops the failing-checks and changes-requested pills the card carries
confirmed.what_user_sees: In card view, VIB-7 shows a red `3/5 checks failing` pill (:327-333) and/or an amber `changes requested` pill (:334-340) in the card foot. The user clicks "List" in the Board/List segmented control (:887-895) — same page, same filter, same tasks — and both pills are gone. The list row renders readiness, the merge-pending/closed PR pill, validation and the wait tag, and nothing else (:538-555). Nothing on the row says the build is broken or that a teammate asked for changes on the PR.
confirmed.why_wrong: These are two views of one surface, and the card's own comment justifies both pills as the ACTIONABLE state a supervisor needs off the board: "a failing build on a task sitting in Review is [news]" and "a teammate asking for changes on the PR is the case a supervisor needs off the board". F19-13 fixed precisely this class one pill earlier in this same pass — the list row had been dropping the merge-pending/closed PR pills, and the fix comment (:539-543) states the rule: "One board, two views, one vocabulary". Checks and review state were left behind by the same reasoning that condemned the PR pills.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add the two conditional pills to the list row inside the non-archived branch, in the card's order (PR state → checks → review → validation → wait): `{t.prChecks?.state === "failing" && …checksPill…}` and `{t.prReview === "changes_requested" && …reviewPill…}`, reusing `checksPill`/`reviewPill` from `~/features/github/github-pills` exactly as the card does.
corrections: Real but keep it narrow and LOW, exactly the F19-13 class, not a new severity. Accurate claim: the board's list row omits the two ACTIONABLE PR-state pills the card foot draws — failing checks (board-page.tsx:327-331) and GitHub `changes_requested` (:334-338) — so a task with a broken build or a teammate's change request looks the same as a clean one in List view (:530-557). Two details in the write-up need trimming: (a) the anchor line should be board-page.tsx:530-557 (the live-state block); :528 is `OwnerLine`. (b) "and nothing else" overstates — the row also carries the key link, title, StageMenu/stage pill, OwnerLine and ReviewerStack; and the list row is already a deliberately reduced surface in one respect the finding does not acknowledge (it draws no branch chip and no `#124` PR-number chip, which the card does at :280-295). That reduction is defensible under the card's own rule because trace chips are not actionable state — which is precisely why the two pills at issue, which ARE actionable state by the card's stated rule, do not belong in the same reduction. Fix is the one-line mirror of F19-13: reuse `checksPill`/`reviewPill` under the same conditions inside the non-archived branch of `ListView`, ordered as on the card (PR state → checks → review → validation → wait).

Two tightenings to the claim as written. (1) The card-side line numbers are :326-340 (checks pill :327-333, review pill :334-340) and the list-row pill block is :535-556 — cite board-page.tsx:538-555 for the omission rather than :528, which is `OwnerLine`. (2) Frame it as the unfinished half of F19-13, not a new class of defect: pass 19 already ruled the two views must share one vocabulary and fixed `prStatePill` in the list row (:539-547) while leaving `checksPill`/`reviewPill` — which the pass-19 audit record named in the same breath — untouched. The strongest part of the failure story is not just the view-switch: it is that the list row's ValidationPill cannot stand in, because `validation` is task-row state (task.server.ts:303) with no CI input, and the "Blocked or waiting" filter (board-filters.ts:41-62) does not select on prChecks or prReview either — so in List view a red build and a teammate's changes-requested are invisible on every route the board offers.

confirmed.title: The Agents live roster reports "packet open" for every operator on a human-waiting task, including the documented class of task that has no packet at all
confirmed.what_user_sees: VIB-9 sits at Review needing a maintainer's acceptance; no decision packet was ever opened. The board card says "waiting on a human"; the review queue subline says "Waiting at the review boundary — needs a human decision"; the task page shows "Waiting on: Human decision" and renders no Decision packet section. The Agents → Live roster row for that task's operator shows an amber `packet open` pill (agents-page.tsx:968-970), and the page-level stat counts it under "agent threads waiting on a human · this project". A user who clicks that row expecting a packet lands on a task with no packet anywhere on it.
confirmed.why_wrong: `operatorStatus` derives the label from `task.waiting` alone: `waiting === "human" ? "packet open" : "coordinating"`. Two server modules explicitly document that human-waiting is NOT the same as packet-present: review-queue.server.ts:143-146 ("a review-stage task waiting on a human can have no packet/recommendation … yet still need a human to accept it") and decisions.server.ts:126-129 ("B-FD5: acceptance-ready review-stage tasks — the class that carries no decision OBJECT"). The roster is the only surface that names an artifact instead of the state, so one waiting-on-human state renders as "waiting on a human" on the board, "needs a human decision" in the queue, "Human decision" on the task, and "packet open" here — and only the last one can be false. The mirror half is the `else` branch: `coordinating` (agent-tinted, and pulsing via `deploymentDot`, agent-types.ts:139-141) is asserted for an operator on a task whose `waiting` is `none`, i.e. a task the board draws with no wait tag at all and the task page calls "Waiting on: Nothing".
confirmed.suggested_fix: The row already carries the honest facts. Use `task.packet` presence for "packet open" and fall back to the same wording the rest of the app uses ("waiting on human") when a human-waiting task has no packet; use the row's existing `running` flag (populated from the `agent_runs` join at :95-101) to distinguish a genuinely active operator from an idle one instead of asserting "coordinating" for every non-human-waiting task.
corrections: Narrow to the "packet open" half only. Accurate claim: the Agents → Live roster is the one surface that names an ARTIFACT instead of the state — app/server/projections/agent-deployments.server.ts:43-45 labels every operator on a waiting=human task "packet open" without checking packet presence, so the documented no-packet acceptance-ready class (R8-3 / B-FD5 / ruling 48's supervised path) shows an amber "packet open" pill and clicking through lands the user on a task page that renders no decision packet at all (task-detail-page.tsx:418 gates the section on task.packet). The fix is a state-named label consistent with the board/queue/task page, or a packet_json check in the projection. DROP two parts of the original finding: (1) the page-level stat at agents-page.tsx:1100/1268 ("agent threads waiting on a human · this project") is CORRECT — that thread genuinely is waiting on a human, so counting it there is honest and is not part of the defect; (2) the "coordinating" mirror half does not hold — "coordinating" names the operator's standing activity rather than an artifact, so it cannot be false the way "packet open" can. That waiting="none" also yields "coordinating" with a pulsing dot (deploymentDot, agent-types.ts:139-141) is at most a minor liveness overstatement, not a vocabulary contradiction, and should not be filed alongside the artifact-naming defect.

Two adjustments to the claim as written. (1) The page-level stat is not part of the defect: agents-page.tsx:1100-1102 and its label at :1268 ("agent threads waiting on a human · this project") count status "waiting on human" OR "packet open", and the task genuinely IS waiting on a human — that number is honest. Only the per-row "packet open" pill (agents-page.tsx:968-970, fed by agent-deployments.server.ts:44) is false. (2) The destination is not a total dead end — the task page still renders its acceptance panel — so the failure is vocabulary dishonesty rather than a blocked user: "packet"/"Decision packet" names a first-class object with its own section, notification kind and review-queue subline, so the roster sends the user hunting for a section that does not exist on that task, and the Decisions surfaces (decisions.server.ts:117) simultaneously list nothing for it. Also note the trigger is broader than Review: any non-terminal stage (Ready, Impl) whose operator turn ends without opening a packet shows the same pill.

confirmed.what_user_sees: A user hits ⌘K and types a task title. Under "Tasks" they get `VIB-3 · Fix the retry loop` with the project name underneath — identical in every respect to a live task. VIB-3 was archived last week. The same query files its branch under "Branches" with no marker either. Every other surface tells the user: the board card and list row render a neutral `archived` pill instead of live state (board-page.tsx:266-270, :531-534), the task hero renders a lock + "archived" pill, the review queue and decisions inbox drop the task entirely, and the Agents live roster excludes it in SQL (agent-deployments.server.ts:73-74).
confirmed.why_wrong: The task-hit SELECT filters only on project scope and the LIKE terms — no `AND archived = 0` and no archived column read — and the hit shape carries no state field (`sub` is filled with the project name only, :110). Ruling 3's R14-3 line is that an archived task is "a terminal disposition … they leave every default view"; `listProjectTasks` centralises that exclusion so "every other read model … inherits [it] by going through here" (board-query.server.ts:141-144). The palette is the one reader that queries `task_projections` directly and therefore inherits nothing. F19-8 spent this pass making "archived" render identically on card, list row and hero; search is the remaining surface where the state is simply absent.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Select `archived` alongside the existing columns and either append a state marker to the hit's `sub` (e.g. `${project} · archived`) for archived rows, or sort them last — do not silently exclude them, since the palette is a legitimate way back to archived work and R14-3 keeps the record reachable. Apply the same to the branch hits built from the same rows (:114-127).
corrections: Narrow it to a labeling/coherence gap, not a dishonest affordance or dead end, and drop two overstatements. (1) The palette shows NO task state for ANY hit — no stage, no readiness, no merge-pending — so archived is not singled out for omission; the accurate claim is that a terminal disposition which R14-3 removes from every default view is ranked in ⌘K (ORDER BY updated_at DESC, so a just-archived task ranks first) indistinguishably from live work, while the same query already SELECTs `stage` (line 88) and throws it away. (2) It is not a dead end: Enter lands on the task page, which immediately renders the lock + `archived` pill and disables the move controls, so the user is corrected in one click — the cost is a wasted jump and a moment of false "this is live", not a wrong action. (3) "The one reader that queries task_projections directly and inherits nothing" is too strong — notifications.server.ts:198 also LEFT JOINs `task_projections` with no archived filter (defensible, since that inbox is a historical event feed). The minimal honest fix is a marker on the hit (reuse the neutral `archived` pill / put it in `sub`), not exclusion — search is a legitimate way back to archived work.

Two supporting citations in the claim are wrong and must be fixed before filing. (1) `agent-deployments.server.ts:73-74` does not exist in the repo — the Agents roster read model is app/features/agents/agents-query.server.ts, which contains no archived handling at all, so "the Agents live roster excludes it in SQL" is unverified and should be dropped. (2) The review queue does not filter archived itself (app/server/projections/review-queue.server.ts has no `archived` reference); it excludes archived tasks indirectly through listProjectTasks' default at app/server/projections/board-query.server.ts:164 (`${opts.includeArchived ? "" : "AND archived = 0"}`). The verified comparison set is: board card (board-page.tsx:266-270), board list row (:530-534), home project cards (home-query.server.ts:157,184), decisions inbox (decisions.server.ts:105,122,135), review queue (via board-query.server.ts:164), and task detail (task-detail-page.tsx:231-236). Strengthen the finding by citing the two in-repo statements of the contract the palette breaks: db/migrations/0001_baseline.sql:85-87 ("each of them has to hide archived tasks") and board-page.tsx:820-822 ("archived tasks are out of every other view; this is the way back to them").

confirmed.title: "Confirm decision" deletes the remote branch with no confirmation and no disclosure dialog
confirmed.what_user_sees: A closed-PR recovery packet (ruling 17) opens on the task with three options; the operator's recommended pick is pre-selected because `sel` initialises to `p.options.findIndex(o => o.rec)` (decision-packet.tsx:107-109). When that pick is `archive_task` with `deleteBranch: true`, the only disclosure is a small "deletes branch" pill on the option row (:257-262). One click on the primary button labelled "Confirm decision" fires `onResolve(sel, note)` (:329), which `task-detail-page.tsx:369-386` posts straight to the server for every kind except `accept_completion`. The server archives the task and then permanently deletes the remote GitHub branch (`task-actions.server.ts:4838-4884`, delete at :4846 via `deleteTaskRemoteBranch`). The user learns it happened from a timeline note afterwards.
confirmed.why_wrong: Every other one-way write on this page now asks first. Ruling 20 (R15-1) requires a confirm dialog on every acceptance path and pass 19 closed the last four gaps in that family (rec-Apply, packet option, Stage-dropdown, board drag) — F19-7 specifically added the routing at task-detail-page.tsx:377-386 so that a packet option that merges cannot fire from "Confirm decision". The archive half of the same packet has its own disclosure dialog (`archive-confirm.tsx`, which enumerates what is withdrawn) when reached from the Current-state "Archive task" button, and that path does not even delete a branch. So the *least* destructive archive path confirms and the *most* destructive one — the only remote-branch deletion the product has (ruling 17: "Remote-branch deletion exists only as that packet resolution") — does not. The label "Confirm decision" also names no outcome, violating the UX spec's rule that a button label describes the outcome.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror the F19-7 pattern: in `task-detail-page.tsx`'s `onResolve`, intercept `option.kind === "archive_task" && option.deleteBranch` the same way `accept_completion` is intercepted, and route it into a confirm that names the branch (`task.branch`), states that deleting it on GitHub cannot be undone, and states what archiving withdraws — reusing `ArchiveConfirm` with a branch-deletion block is the smallest change. Keep the plain `archive_task` option firing directly only if you also route it through `ArchiveConfirm`; at minimum the `deleteBranch` variant must not commit from a bare click.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: resolving an `archive_task` packet option — including the `deleteBranch: true` variant, the product's only remote-branch deletion (ruling 17) — is the one irreversible write on the task page that reaches the server without the confirm step its own sibling control uses. ArchiveConfirm (`archive-confirm.tsx:36-45`) exists specifically to name what the archive WITHDRAWS (the open decision, and "N pending operator recommendations"); on the packet path the open decision is self-evidently being resolved, but the pending-recommendation withdrawal is disclosed nowhere before the click, and neither is the branch deletion's irreversibility. Drop two parts of the original: (1) the "Confirm decision" label complaint is already-settled ground — F17-L8 asked for the echo, it was implemented, then narrowed to `aria-label={`Confirm decision: ${selected.t}`}` because echoing a multi-line option title overflowed the flex button and self-overlapped (F-UI1); the code documents that at decision-packet.tsx:322-340, so re-filing it is noise. (2) "the only disclosure is a small pill" overstates it: the option carries an operator-authored title and detail, the operator is prompted to NAME the branch in the packet body and options (`operator-run.server.ts:2213`, `operator-actions.server.ts:1408-1410`, `:1544-1547`), and the row shows a red `Pill kind="blocked"` "deletes branch" (decision-packet.tsx:253-262). The user is told deletion is on the table; what is missing is a confirmation step and the withdrawal disclosure, not the fact. Also note the pre-selection is conditional, not guaranteed: the operator authors which option is `recommended` (rework is the prompted default unless the work is rejected outright), and `operator-actions.server.ts:781` falls back to marking option 0 recommended when none is.

Two framings in the claim need tightening, and the real defect should be stated as a coherence contradiction rather than a bare missing dialog.

1. "The operator's recommended pick is pre-selected [and] when that pick is archive_task with deleteBranch" overstates the default. operator-run.server.ts:2214 tells the operator to "Mark exactly one option recommended (rework, unless the timeline shows the work was rejected outright)", so the destructive option is pre-selected only in the rejected-outright case; otherwise the user must click the option first, then Confirm. Pre-selection is an aggravator, not the core of the finding.

2. "no confirmation and no disclosure" is too absolute. There IS a deliberate disclosure — the "deletes branch" Pill at decision-packet.tsx:257-262, pinned by task-detail-components.test.tsx:1268 — and selecting a radio then pressing Confirm is itself two clicks. What is absent is a confirm STEP that names the branch and says the deletion is one-way.

The accurate finding: on one task page, Viberr confirms the reversible archive and does not confirm the irreversible one. Archive task (keeps the branch, restorable) routes through ArchiveConfirm, which names the stage, the PR state and the pending question it withdraws. The packet option "Archive and delete the branch" — the same archive PLUS a permanent remote-branch delete carrying the only copy of the rejected work — commits from a button labelled "Confirm decision" that names neither the branch nor the deletion, and the user first learns the outcome from a timeline note written afterwards (task-actions.server.ts:4862-4884). That inverts the app's own escalation of ceremony with destructiveness, and it is the same class pass 19 just closed for the acceptance family (F19-7: a one-way write must not commit from the packet card's generic "Confirm decision" without stating what it destroys). The consistent fix is the existing pattern — route archive_task with deleteBranch through a confirm that names the branch, says deletion is permanent, and offers a "Not yet" — not a new mechanism.

confirmed.title: The scheduled operator re-run offers a backend the deployment has no credential for, one panel below a picker that disables it
confirmed.what_user_sees: In "Scheduled re-runs" the Backend `<select>` lists "Claude Code" and "Codex" unconditionally (task-main-sections.tsx:400-405). On a deployment where only one backend is configured, a maintainer picks the unconfigured one, gets the toast "Scheduled · operator re-run in 60 min" (`project.task.tsx:778`), and nothing looks wrong. Hours later, unwatched, the runner fires it, `selectAdapter` returns `{kind:"unavailable"}` (`runtime-registry.server.ts:585`), the run fails, and `escalateFailedOperatorRun` opens a blocked packet reading "the coordinating backend has no usable credential configured (the run was refused — no agent process started)" (`operator-run.server.ts:1805-1806`). The user is now debugging a failure they scheduled and could not have predicted.
confirmed.why_wrong: The identical control for an *immediate* operator run sits a few hundred pixels above in the same page, and it is honest: `OperatorRunControl` disables the unavailable option and appends "— not configured" to its label (`execution-profile.tsx:479-484`), and even re-defaults the picker away from an unavailable backend (:459-466, "so the picker never starts on an option that would fail fast"). The loader already ships `backendAvailable` for exactly this (`project.task.tsx:247-250`) and `ScheduledActions` is simply never handed it. Server-side nothing catches it either: `scheduleTaskAction` validates `dueAt` and the terminal stage but never backend availability (`schedule.server.ts:139-152`). FR39 exists precisely so an agent can act with no human present, which makes the un-disclosed dead option worse here than on the immediate control.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Thread `backendAvailable` from the loader through `task-detail-page.tsx` into `ScheduledActions` and give the schedule form the same option treatment as `OperatorRunControl`: `disabled={!backendAvailable.codex}` with a "— not configured" label suffix, and default the select to a configured backend. Additionally have `scheduleTaskAction` refuse an unavailable backend with a validation error, so the file can never carry a schedule that is guaranteed to fail.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the "Scheduled re-runs" backend picker (app/features/task-detail/task-main-sections.tsx:396-405) offers both backends unconditionally, while the immediate operator run picker on the same page disables the unconfigured one and labels it "— not configured" (app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx:456-484) from data the loader already ships (app/routes/project.task.tsx:247-250) and simply never passes down (app/features/task-detail/task-detail-page.tsx:448-452). Two corrections to the claim as written: (1) the direction is inverted — ScheduledActions renders ABOVE ExecutionSection (task-detail-page.tsx:448 before :454), so the honest picker is below the blind one, not above it; (2) the failure is not undiscoverable or unrecoverable. It escalates into a blocked decision packet titled "Operator run failed — pick a recovery path" whose body names the concrete next steps ("Retry on the other backend, fix the credential, or redirect the task", operator-run.server.ts:1815-1823), and the same instance-level fact is already disclosed on the agents page ("Codex — not configured", "…is not configured on this instance — runs for this profile would fail", agents-page.tsx:175/640/802) and one panel down on the task page. So the user is not left without a signal; the defect is that one control silently accepts a choice its twin refuses, deferring a knowable-at-click-time refusal into a delayed unattended failure that must be cleared through a packet. Severity is a coherence/honest-affordance defect, not a blocking dead end.

Two corrections, both strengthening the finding. (1) The user does not have to actively pick the unconfigured backend: the schedule select is defaultValue="claude" (task-main-sections.tsx:401) with no availability fallback, whereas OperatorRunControl one panel below falls back to an available backend (execution-profile.tsx:456-467). On a Codex-only instance the two pickers on the same screen default to DIFFERENT backends, and the schedule form's default is the one that cannot run — so the failure is the path of least resistance, not a misclick. (2) Line-number drift: the toast is project.task.tsx:781 (not 778), selectAdapter's unavailable return is runtime-registry.server.ts:585-586, and the anchor for the finding is task-main-sections.tsx:401 (the select itself) with the missing prop at :297-301.

confirmed.title: The delete-profile dialog promises engaged threads "keep running", which ruling 26 (R15-7) makes false
confirmed.what_user_sees: Deleting a deployed agent profile that is engaged on live tasks opens a confirm reading: "It is currently engaged on N active tasks — those threads keep running until the operator reassigns them." (agents-page.tsx:294-300). The admin confirms, expecting continuity. In fact `deleteAgentProfile` only removes the deployment from `project.md` (`agent-profile-actions.server.ts:635-637`); the engagements stay in every task file as unresolvable ghosts. The next run of any of them resolves nothing (`specialist-run.server.ts:723-731`), takes `resolveUndeployedDisallowedTools()` (:760) and `withheldAgentGrants()` (:832) — so it cannot write the repo, cannot deliver, cannot post a comment, cannot ask a human, and cannot attach evidence. The thread "runs" and produces nothing anyone can act on.
confirmed.why_wrong: Ruling 26 (R15-7) is explicit: "A run whose profile can no longer be resolved gets nothing permissive — no delivery, no comments, no ask-human, no evidence." The dialog is the last guardrail before an irreversible policy change and it states the opposite of the ruling that governs the outcome. It also names a recovery — "until the operator reassigns them" — that no surface promises: reassignment of a delivering engagement is a human action from the Execution profile's "Assign delivering agent" menu, and there is no operator behaviour that re-points an existing ghost engagement.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Rewrite the `activeCount > 0` branch to state what R15-7 actually does, e.g. "It is engaged on N active tasks. Those engagements stay on the tasks but stop being able to deliver, comment, ask a human or record evidence — assign a replacement delivering agent on each task." Do not restate reassignment as automatic.
corrections:
Narrower accurate claim: the delete-profile confirm (app/features/agents/agents-page.tsx:292-300) and its success toast (app/routes/project.agents.tsx:179) promise continuity — "those threads keep running until the operator reassigns them" — for a count that is ENGAGEMENTS, not live runs. Two things are wrong, and one thing in the original finding is not:

1. "keep running" is true only of a run already in flight (deletion aborts nothing). For every engagement that is idle — which is most of what `activeCount` counts — nothing is running, and the NEXT run is a fully-withheld ghost run under ruling 26: it starts, but cannot deliver, comment, ask a human or attach evidence (specialist-run.server.ts:760, :832; capability-catalog.ts:90-95). The admin's last guardrail says "fine, work continues"; the runtime says "work continues in a form that can produce nothing anyone can act on".

2. Nothing anywhere marks the resulting engagement as unresolvable — not the task's Execution panel, which silently falls back to the stored `role` label (execution-profile.tsx:598-601) — and nothing wakes the operator on deletion (deleteAgentProfile only edits project.md, reprojects, audits). So the recovery the copy promises is not scheduled by anything; it happens only if a human notices and acts.

3. DROP the claim that "there is no operator behaviour that re-points an existing ghost engagement." That is false. The operator's `engage_agent` tool with `delivers: true` (app/server/tasks/operator-toolkit.server.ts:372-396) routes to `operatorEngageAgent` → `operatorAssignSpecialist` (operator-actions.server.ts:2157-2185, 1759-1795) → `assignSpecialist` (specialist-run.server.ts:344-460), which performs a real deliverer handoff, replaces the engagement, and writes a "Delivery handed off from X to Y" timeline event — directly under full autonomy, as an "Assign … as the delivering agent" recommendation card under supervised. The mechanism exists; the defect is that the copy asserts it will happen automatically when nothing triggers it, and that it describes the interim state as healthy when ruling 26 makes it inert.

Keep the finding, with two adjustments. (1) It is not only about "deployed agent engaged on LIVE tasks" — `activeCount` counts engagements on every non-archived, non-terminal task (agent-deployments.server.ts:60-150), including idle "anchored · on call" reviewers, so the misleading branch fires in the common case, not just mid-run. (2) Drop the implication that reassignment does not exist: `assignSpecialist` (app/server/tasks/specialist-run.server.ts:344) is a real admin/maintainer action and a real operator recommendation kind. The defect is the two promises — that the threads "keep running" (they run, but per ruling 26 they can no longer deliver, comment, ask a human, or attach evidence) and that "the operator reassigns them" (delete queues no operator run, writes no task timeline event, and sends no notification, so nothing initiates the handoff). Fix both strings together: app/features/agents/agents-page.tsx:294-300 and the success toast at app/routes/project.agents.tsx:179. Honest copy states the consequence and names the human's next step, e.g. "It is currently engaged on N active tasks. Those engagements stay on the tasks, but until someone assigns a replacement, runs there can't deliver, comment, ask a question, or attach evidence." A stronger fix also makes the ghost visible on the task itself, since execution-profile.tsx:600-601 currently falls back to the role label with no indication the profile is gone.

confirmed.title: Task detail keeps a live "Run" button for an engagement whose profile no longer exists, while the Agents page names the condition
confirmed.what_user_sees: After a profile is deleted (or re-deployed elsewhere), the task's Execution profile still renders the delivering agent and each reviewer as a healthy row: `agentNameOf` silently falls back to the engagement's `role` string when the profile is not in `deployedSpecialists` (execution-profile.tsx:600-601), and the "Run" button stays enabled — it is disabled only for `runBusy || deliveringActive || closed` (:687, and :745 for reviewers). The user clicks Run, the run starts and streams, and produces no branch, no PR, no comment, no verdict and no evidence, because the run took the fully-withheld posture (`specialist-run.server.ts:760`, `:832`). Nothing on the page said the profile was gone.
confirmed.why_wrong: The same fact is disclosed honestly on the Agents page live table, which prints "profile no longer here" with a diagnostic tooltip rather than the raw id, precisely because "the engagement outlived the profile" (agents-page.tsx:894-925). One state, two renderings — a coherence defect — and on the surface where the action lives, the wrong one. This is also the same shape UI-39 already fixed one menu away: the assign menu badges a deployed agent that lacks a repo-write grant with "· no repo write" and explains "its run starts, streams, and produces no branch or PR" (execution-profile.tsx:293-320). A ghost is strictly worse than that case and gets no badge at all.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `ExecutionProfile`, compute `deployed = deployedSpecialists.some(s => s.id === profileId)` for `task.specialist` and each `task.reviewers` entry. When false, render the Agents-page wording ("profile no longer here") as the name, add a rendered sub-line naming the consequence (the run cannot deliver, comment or record a verdict), and disable Run with that reason as visible copy — not a `title`, per the P14 ruling already cited at execution-profile.tsx:513-519.
corrections:
Two narrowings.

(a) "Renders as a healthy row" is slightly strong. The fallback is the engagement's `role`, and the sub-line is `{role} · {backend}` — so a ghost delivering row reads e.g. "Implementation" over "Implementation · Codex", a duplicated-role tell rather than a plausible agent name. It is undisclosed, not disguised.

(b) The UI-39 comparison is menu-vs-row, not row-vs-row. The "· no repo write" badge at execution-profile.tsx:296-320 exists only inside the *assign* menu; once engaged, neither a repo-write-less agent nor a ghost carries any capability badge on its row (:673-701, :729-771). So "a ghost is strictly worse and gets no badge" overstates the asymmetry — no engaged row is badged at all. UI-39 remains the right precedent for the principle (say it where the dead-end action is offered), not for an existing row-level badge that a ghost is missing.

Narrowed accurate claim: on task detail, the Execution profile resolves an engaged profile's name against `deployedSpecialists` and silently substitutes the role string when the profile is gone (execution-profile.tsx:600-601, used at :677 and :735), while leaving Run enabled (:687, :745). The identical condition is named as "profile no longer here" with a diagnostic tooltip on the Agents live table (agents-page.tsx:924-927). A senior engineer clicking Run gets a run that is fully withheld by ruling R15-7 (specialist-run.server.ts:760, :832) — and, separately, a Review push that will refuse (task-actions.server.ts:3388-3392) — with no statement of the cause on the surface that offered the action.

Two refinements worth carrying into the finding.

(a) The contradiction is sharper than "the Agents page names the condition" — the Agents page makes a PROMISE the task page cannot keep. The delete dialog says the threads "keep running until the operator reassigns them", but the task page offers no reassign affordance for a delivering agent at all: `SpecialistControl` is rendered only in the `sp === null` branch (`app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx:667-717`), and the delivering row has no release "×" (only reviewers get one, `:751-760`). So after the delete the task is a dead end: the human cannot reassign, and the only control on offer (Run) starts a run that structurally cannot deliver. There is also no automatic reassignment machinery — grep for reassign across app/ finds only these two copy strings, an operator packet-button example (`operator-toolkit.server.ts:280`), and the users-panel deactivation copy.

(b) One small secondary tell to include: `agentNameOf` falling back to `sp.role` makes the row print the role twice (name line = "Implementation", sub line = "Implementation · Codex"), and the Agent-logs picker labels the run with the raw `profileId` because `agentName` falls back to it (`specialist-run.server.ts:749`). Both are drift symptoms of the same missing state, not disclosures — a user cannot read either as "this profile was deleted".

confirmed.title: The capability picker accepts modes the server silently rewrites, including on the three always-human locks
confirmed.what_user_sees: In the create/edit agent-profile modal, the "Reserved for humans" accordion group renders three rows — Merge a pull request, Transition a task to Done, Change project policy — each with a fully interactive Allowed / Human-only / Off segmented radiogroup (create-profile-modal.tsx:583-604). Nothing is disabled and nothing explains the group is not editable. An admin sets "Merge a pull request" to Allowed, saves, sees a success toast, reopens the profile — and the row reads Human-only again, because the server coerces it unconditionally: `if (ALWAYS_HUMAN.has(capabilityId)) mode = "human"` (`agent-profile-actions.server.ts:185`, and the create path at :239). The same control does it again for "Report a validation verdict": choosing Human-only persists `off` (`agent-profile-actions.server.ts:175-181`, "every other value … persists off"), so a reviewer the admin believed was human-gated is simply ungranted.
confirmed.why_wrong: A control that accepts input and discards it is the purest form of a silent no-op, and it is here on what the code itself calls "the most consequential setting in the product" (the UXA-4 comment at :576-582). The Policy page renders the same three capabilities correctly — a locked, non-interactive "Always reserved for humans" list with a lock icon and a `risk` pill (`policy-page.tsx:331-348`) — so the two surfaces that describe one invariant disagree about whether it is editable. Ruling 2 and `ALWAYS_HUMAN_CAPABILITY_IDS` (`app/shared/capabilities.ts:166-170`) make these a server invariant, not a default the admin may override.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `CapabilityGrants`, mark the rows the server will coerce: for `ALWAYS_HUMAN_CAPABILITY_IDS` render the mode as a static locked value (matching `policy-page.tsx`'s treatment) rather than a radiogroup, or render the radios `aria-disabled` with a rendered line naming the invariant. For `report-validation-verdict`, drop "Human-only" from the offered modes (it is explicit-`direct`-or-nothing) or label the middle option so it matches what is stored. The catalog already carries `promotable: false` on all four ids — key the UI off that instead of leaving the modal ignorant of it.
corrections: Two narrowings. (a) "Nothing explains the group is not editable" is slightly strong: the accordion header does read "Reserved for humans" and the rows seed to Human-only. The defect is not absent labelling but an interactive control that contradicts its own group name — it accepts Allowed/Off, reports success, and silently reverts, while the codebase already has the locked variant of that exact control (`.cap-seg.locked`, app.css:2093, used at policy-page.tsx:471) it simply never applies here. (b) The `report-validation-verdict` half is real but its consequence is misstated: choosing "Human-only" persists `off` (agent-profile-actions.server.ts:175-181, :250-253), which is a genuine round-trip rewrite the UI shows — `capabilitiesToActionLabels` (capabilities.ts:110-128) deliberately buckets `human` ("Reserved for humans") separately from `off` (withheld) per NEW-3, and the policy page counts "N human" from the forbidden bucket — but it does NOT leave the reviewer more powerful or the admin's intent defeated: in both modes the agent holds no verdict authority. So "a reviewer the admin believed was human-gated is simply ungranted" should read: the saved policy displays in a different bucket and count than the admin chose, with no widening of authority. The accurate finding is: the specialist capability picker offers modes the server discards without any notice — on the three always-human locks (coerced to `human`) and on report-validation-verdict (Human-only coerced to `off`) — even though the same control ships a locked, disabled variant used on the Policy page for the same class of invariant.

Two scope notes for the writeup. (1) The "Reserved for humans" group is the LAST accordion group and starts collapsed — only `capCatalog[0].group` ("Repository & execution") is open by default (`create-profile-modal.tsx:819-821`) — so the path costs one extra click; it does not change reachability. (2) The two halves differ in stakes and should be stated separately: the always-human half is a pure honesty/coherence defect (the server invariant holds, so nothing unsafe is ever persisted — the user is merely overruled without being told, while a sibling surface draws the same rows with a lock). The `report-validation-verdict` half is the same silent-rewrite class but with a real consequence worth naming: "Human-only" persists `off` (`agent-profile-actions.server.ts:175-181`, create path `:246-250`), and because verdict authority is snapshotted at engage time from an explicit `direct` grant, an admin who believed they had left review authority "human-gated" simply has an ungranted profile. Do not frame either half as a privilege-escalation bug.

confirmed.title: First-run project creation dead-ends any non-admin: the empty state links them into a 403
confirmed.what_user_sees: A signed-in org MEMBER (not admin) with zero projects lands on Home, sees the EmptyHero "Create your first project" (home-sections.tsx:243) and clicks "New project". Project creation is deliberately self-serve for any member (routes/_index.tsx:172-178), but a repo-bound connection is REQUIRED (project-create.server.ts:206-212). With no connections in the store the modal renders: "No GitHub connections yet — every project needs a repository. Add a PAT in **Instance settings → GitHub connections**, then come back." — with that phrase as a live <Link to="/org/settings?tab=connections">. Clicking it hits requireRole(request,"admin") (routes/org.settings.tsx:71) and the user gets a full-page error. The instruction the empty state gives is one the member cannot carry out, and it offers no other route forward.

Ask an admin to add one, then come back." (no link). Two corrections. (1) It is not first-run-specific: the same modal opens from the toolbar "New project" button (app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:233), so any member on a connectionless instance hits it whether or not they have projects — the EmptyHero is just the likeliest first encounter, not a precondition. confirmed.title: The archived-project banner sends every non-admin to a Danger zone that Q-V1 hid from them
confirmed.what_user_sees: A maintainer (or contributor/viewer) opens an archived project. The full-width banner under the topbar reads: "This project is archived — it's read-only. Timelines and audit stay visible; restore it from Settings → Danger zone to make changes." They click Settings in the rail, land on "<name> · settings", scroll the whole page — Project, Workflow stages, Members, Repository & credentials — and there is no Danger zone panel, no archive control, and no note explaining who can restore it. Home repeats the same instruction to the same users in the Archived section lede (app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:399-400: "Open a project and use Settings → Danger zone to restore it.").
confirmed.why_wrong: The Q-V1 owner ruling (settings-page.tsx:1603) changed DangerZone from "render for everyone, disabled, with a deny note" to `{canEditPolicy && <DangerZone …/>}`, and `edit-policy` is admin-only (app/shared/rbac.ts:78). The two pieces of copy that route users there were not updated with it, so the ruling turned an honest disabled control into a wayfinding dead end: the app names an exact nav destination that does not exist for the reader. It also contradicts the UX spec's recovery rule (ux-design-specification.md:872: "Every recovery pattern should lead users back to a trusted state, not deeper into ambiguity") and the LV-F2/UXA-3 pattern this same pass applied to all four Settings panels — speak to the reader's actual authority.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make both strings role-aware, the same way the LV-F2 lock notes are. In project.tsx the layout loader already returns `myRole`, so render the restore clause only when `roleCan(myRole, "edit-policy")`; otherwise say who can do it — e.g. "…Timelines and audit stay visible. A project admin can restore it from Settings → Danger zone." Do the same for home-sections.tsx:399-400 (the home loader knows the viewer's role per project, or fall back to the neutral admin-naming phrasing).
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the defect is the two pointer strings, not the Q-V1 gate. app/routes/project.tsx:234 and app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:399-400 both instruct every reader to "Settings → Danger zone", but that panel renders only under edit-policy (settings-page.tsx:1603 / rbac.ts edit-policy = admin), so a project maintainer, contributor or viewer follows an exact named path to a panel that is not there and finds no statement of who can restore (the in-panel deny note at settings-page.tsx:1336-1343 is unreachable dead code, since canManageLifecycle at :1321 is the same check as the gate). Scope caveats: org admins are unaffected (the orgAdminOverride resolves them to project admin), and the reader is not stranded on a broken page — the LV-F2/UXA-3 lock notes on Project/Stages/Members/Repo still explain the general read-only state; none of them mentions archive/restore or names the authority. The fix is copy that speaks to the reader's authority (e.g. non-admins told a project admin can restore it), not restoring the Danger zone for non-admins. Severity: low-to-moderate wayfinding/honesty gap, not a blocker.

Two supporting details worth folding into the finding.

(a) The copy is wrong on two surfaces, and the honest instruction differs per role: `app/routes/project.tsx:231-235` and `app/features/home/home-sections.tsx:398-401`. For a non-admin the truthful sentence names the authority, not a route (the app already has this shape elsewhere — e.g. the read-only note at `app/features/project-settings/settings-page.tsx:1338-1344` and the Project panel's "Read-only … Change project settings" note tested at `app/features/project-settings/settings-page.test.tsx:142-155`). Both strings need the role-aware split, or the settings page needs a visible "this project is archived — a project admin can restore it" line for members without `edit-policy`.

(b) Q-V1's gate made an older honesty fix unreachable dead code: `DangerZone` still computes `canManageLifecycle = roleCan(myRole, "edit-policy")` (`settings-page.tsx:1329`) and renders the P14-LV-08 deny note "Archiving and deleting {projectName} need the **Edit workflow & policy** grant — ask a project admin" (lines 1337-1344), plus `disabled`/`title` fallbacks at 1360-1362 and 1374-1376. Since the parent gates the entire panel on that identical `edit-policy` check (line 1603), `canManageLifecycle` is always true when the panel renders — the deny note and the disabled states can never appear. That note's text is precisely the explanation the stranded maintainer needs; it is currently rendered nowhere.

confirmed.title: A ⌘K agent hit opens the Agents page on a different agent than the one that was picked
confirmed.what_user_sees: A senior engineer presses ⌘K, types "reviewer", sees the Agents group with the row "Reviewer Bot — reviewer · Viberr Core", and hits Enter. The Agents page loads with the tab set to Profiles and the detail pane showing the **Operator** profile. Nothing on the page indicates which agent they searched for; they have to re-find "Reviewer Bot" in the roster list and click it. The same happens for every agent hit in the palette.
confirmed.why_wrong: The palette's whole contract is "Enter navigates to the hit's own surface" (command-palette.tsx:11-15). The Agents page already has real, linkable selection state — `sel = searchParams.get("profile") ?? "operator"` (agents-page.tsx:1040), written back on every click with `replace: true` precisely so a selection is bookmarkable/linkable — and `agent.id` from `listDeployedSpecialists` is `resolved.profileId` (specialist-run.server.ts:2162), the same id space as `AgentProfileView.id` (agents-query.server.ts:309). The hit therefore has everything it needs to land in context and throws it away, producing a deep link that lands without context.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Emit the selection in the href: `href: `/projects/${project.slug}/agents?profile=${encodeURIComponent(agent.id)}`` at command-search.server.ts:150. No page change is needed — agents-page.tsx:1040 already reads `?profile=`.
corrections: Narrow it from "the palette's contract is broken" to an inconsistency with the app's own deep-link idiom. An agent has no per-agent route, so the Agents page IS the hit's surface, and branch hits likewise land on the task page with no in-page anchor — the palette's "Enter navigates to the hit's own surface" docstring is not literally violated. The accurate claim: the ⌘K agent hit is the only hit kind that discards identity the destination can consume. It links to the bare roster (`/projects/<slug>/agents`) rather than `?profile=<agent.id>`, the deep link policy-page.tsx:611 already uses for "open this profile" as distinct from "manage profiles". The user who picked "Reviewer Bot" lands with the Operator's detail pane open and no indication of what they searched for. Severity is low: recovery is one click on a roster already on screen, so this is missed-context friction and vocabulary-of-navigation drift, not a dead end or a dishonest affordance.

The finding stands as written; two precisions worth carrying into the report. (1) The mis-landing is deterministic, not incidental: the palette only ever emits specialist hits, and the page's fallback is operator-first, so the pane shows the operator on every single agent hit — there is no case where the user happens to land on the right agent. (2) The fix is a one-line href change with an identifier already available at the call site: `/projects/${project.slug}/agents?profile=${agent.id}`, since `agent.id` is `resolved.profileId` (specialist-run.server.ts:2162), the same key the roster resolves against (agents-query.server.ts:309), and the same shape policy-page.tsx:611 already uses. Note the claim's mention of the Profiles tab is not itself a defect — Profiles is the correct default (`tab` only becomes "live" on explicit `?tab=live`).

confirmed.title: /notifications says "all caught up" and withdraws Mark all read while unread rows are still on screen
confirmed.what_user_sees: After a project directory is removed from the file store out of band (the file-native workflow FR10 supports) and the store is re-scanned, the escalation engineer opens the bell — no badge — then "See all". The page header reads "Everything routed to you, across all projects · all caught up", and there is no "Mark all read" button. Below it, the Everything else stream still shows three rows carrying unread dots, an explicit "Mark read" button each, and the note "project no longer exists". Switching the filter to **Unread** shows those same rows under a header that still claims everything is caught up. They can only be cleared one at a time.
confirmed.why_wrong: `countUnreadNotifications` deliberately excludes rows whose project is gone (notifications.server.ts:246-252, F18-1, so the badge is not inflated), but `listNotifications` still returns them with `unread: true` and the renderer still draws them as unread (notification-item.tsx:48, notifications-page.tsx:186-199). F18-1 fixed the badge and the row, not the header count or the bulk action that both read the same number — so one page states two different answers to "is there anything unread?", and the affordance that would resolve it (`unread > 0 &&` at :274) is gated on the number that says no.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Have the page count what it renders. Either derive the header/bulk-action number from the items on screen (`items.filter(n => n.unread).length`) while keeping the bell badge on the orphan-excluding count, or return both figures from the loader and render "N unread · M in projects that no longer exist". Keep Mark all read visible whenever any rendered row is unread — the read-all action already clears these rows, only its trigger is hidden.
corrections: Narrower accurate claim: the unread *count* and the unread *rows* disagree on two surfaces, not one, and the cited row file is wrong. (a) The /notifications page's stream rows are notifications-page.tsx:159-203 (dot at :199, "Mark read" at :186-198, orphan note via keybtnLabel :33-37) — notification-item.tsx:48 is the BELL POPOVER's shared row, which has the identical defect: top-bell.tsx:130-134 prints "caught up" and withdraws its own "Mark all read" off the same excluded count while rendering orphan rows with unread dots. Both read countUnreadNotifications (routes/notifications.tsx:44, project.tsx:134, _index.tsx:56). (b) The "no badge / all caught up" phrasing holds only when EVERY unread row is an orphan; in a mixed set the header instead undercounts ("2 unread" beside 5 visible dots) — still a contradiction, milder. (c) markAllNotificationsRead (notifications.server.ts:286-294) has no project filter, so the bulk action would in fact clear orphans — the bug is purely the `unread > 0 &&` gating that hides it, not the action's behavior. (d) On the page a stream row also marks read on plain click (:162), so clearing is one-per-row but not button-precision-dependent.

Narrow the claim on four points. (1) Trigger: the in-app "Delete project" cannot produce it (settings-actions.server.ts:814 deletes the project's notification rows); the only path is out-of-band removal OR rename of the project directory in the store, then the boot rescan / watcher (rebuilder.server.ts:158). (2) It is not a surface-to-surface inconsistency — the bell popover says the same thing (top-bell.tsx:130 "caught up", :132-136 hides Mark all read) while notification-item.tsx:64 still draws the unread dot on orphans; one miscount, rendered consistently in two places. (3) Not a hard dead end: clicking anywhere on an unread stream row marks it read (notifications-page.tsx:162), so it is one click per row, not only the explicit button — the defect is the withheld bulk control plus the contradictory header, which bites in proportion to how much history the removed project had. (4) The verbatim "all caught up" wording requires the orphans to be the viewer's ONLY unread rows; with live unread rows present the same bug renders as a header count lower than the number of dots on screen.

confirmed.title: Task detail's three ownership/assignment popovers declare role="menu" with no keyboard contract and drop focus on close — the exact defect UI-45 fixed in the account menu
confirmed.what_user_sees: On a task page, "Manage" (ownership, :151→:160), "Assign a delivering agent" (:281→:291) and "Engage a reviewer" (:384→:391) open popovers marked `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` children. A screen reader announces "menu" and its user presses Down-arrow to walk the items: nothing happens — the file contains no `onKeyDown` and no `.focus()` call anywhere (verified: `grep -n "onKeyDown|\.focus()" app/features/task-detail/execution-profile.tsx` returns nothing). Focus never enters the popover, so reaching "Hand off to Elif" needs Tab through the trigger into the list, and the roles say otherwise. Worse, when the popover closes — Escape via `useDismiss`, or after picking an item — the focused menuitem is unmounted with no focus restoration, so focus falls back to `<body>` and the keyboard user is dumped at the top of the document mid-workflow.
confirmed.why_wrong: The same product already ruled on this shape twice, and both rulings are cited in code. `app/features/shell/user-menu.tsx:120` (UI-45): "this declared `role=\"menu\"` / `role=\"menuitem\"` with NO arrow-key handling — a broken ARIA menu contract, which tells a screen-reader user to expect Up/Down navigation that does not exist" — and the fix there was to DROP the roles. `app/features/activity/activity-page.tsx:313` and `notifications-page.tsx:247` (UI-58) did the same for radiogroups. `app/ui/stage-menu.tsx:107-141` implements the full contract (Arrow wrap, Home/End, Escape) and `:90-95` names the focus rule explicitly: "F10-25: close the menu AND return focus to the trigger (keyboard users must not be dumped at the top of the document after Escape / selection)". `settings-page.tsx:365` even documents itself as "Same contract as StageMenu". Three of the app's menus honour the contract, three on the most consequential surface don't — and `app/ui/use-dismiss.ts:6-13` says all seven were converted to the shared dismiss hook precisely so "the same gesture" stops "behav[ing] differently depending on which menu was open." INTENT.md §Accessibility: "keyboard access to every packet action… Inaccessible state is untrustworthy state."
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pick one of the two precedents per menu. Cheapest and consistent with UI-45: drop `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"` from all three (`:160`, `:291`, `:391` and their `menu-item` buttons), give the popover `tabIndex={-1}` + `aria-label`, focus it on open and return focus to the trigger on close — i.e. copy `user-menu.tsx` wholesale. If the roles should stay, lift StageMenu's `onMenuKeyDown` + `closeAndReturnFocus` into a shared `app/ui/roving-menu.ts` next to `roving-radio.ts` and wire all three. Either way, add the focus-return: it is a separate bug from the arrow keys and bites every keyboard user, not only AT users.
corrections: Real, with three details narrowed. (1) The quoted names are aria-labels, not visible copy: the triggers read "Manage" (:151), "Assign delivering agent" (:284) and "Engage reviewer" (:384); "Assign a delivering agent"/"Engage a reviewer" are the panel aria-labels. (2) The count is not "three honour, three don't": exactly two menus implement the contract (stage-menu.tsx, settings-page.tsx's StageMoveMenu) and a third (user-menu.tsx, UI-45) deliberately dropped the roles instead — so of the four `role="menu"` sites in the app, only these three lack the contract, and the product has already ruled twice that the shape must be either implemented or the roles removed. (3) The activity-page/notifications-page citation (UI-58) is the `role="radiogroup"` pattern with the UXA-7 roving-radio helper — corroborating precedent for "don't declare a contract you don't implement", not the same contract. The user-visible failure is narrower than "the menu is unusable": items ARE reachable by Tab (the panel follows the trigger in DOM order), so the two concrete defects are (a) a screen reader announces a menu and Up/Down do nothing, and (b) after Escape or after picking an item, keyboard focus is lost to <body> mid-workflow instead of returning to the trigger.

Two precision fixes so the finding isn't overstated, and one addition:

1. "Focus never enters the popover" overstates it. Unlike UI-45's popovers (top-bell / user-menu are rendered BEFORE their trigger in the DOM, which is why Tab left the menu entirely and why an explicit `.focus()` was required), these three panels are rendered AFTER their trigger (:158→:159, :289→:290, :389→:390), so plain Tab does reach the items. The defect is not unreachable items — it is (a) `role="menu"`/`role="menuitem"` announcing an arrow-key contract the code does not honour, and (b) no focus restoration on close.

2. The focus-drop is real but conditional: it only bites a user who has actually tabbed INTO the panel. Escape from the trigger (the common case) leaves focus on the trigger, since the trigger never lost it. Once focus is on a `.menu-item`, both exits — Escape via useDismiss and activating an item (`setOpen(false)` at :167, :183, :200, :217, :310, :415) — unmount the focused element with no restore, so `document.activeElement` falls back to `<body>` mid-workflow.

3. Worth naming the in-repo remedy rather than leaving it open: the codebase has already settled this twice in opposite directions, and either is acceptable — drop the roles as user-menu.tsx:119-134 did (small button group, plain Tab order is a contract the code honours), or implement them as stage-menu.tsx:94-134 and settings-page.tsx:401-461 do (roving focus, Home/End, focus return to the trigger). What cannot stand is the third state these three menus are in.

confirmed.title: The capability-policy radiogroup added by UXA-4 never got the arrow keys UXA-7 added to its twin — the group promises traversal that does not exist
confirmed.what_user_sees: In New/Edit agent profile → Capability policy, each capability row renders `<div className="cap-seg" role="radiogroup" aria-label={`Policy for ${capDef.label}`}>` with four `role="radio"` buttons (:589-596). A screen reader announces "Policy for Merge pull request, radio group, Human-only, 3 of 4" and the user presses Left/Right: focus does not move. There is no `onKeyDown` and no `tabIndex={checked ? 0 : -1}`, so every radio is also its own tab stop — an expanded capability group with 6 capabilities is 24 Tab presses instead of 6. `app/features/org-settings/resource-modals.tsx:344-367` has the identical defect (`role="radiogroup"` "How the skill gets its content", two `role="radio"` buttons, no keys, no roving tabindex).
confirmed.why_wrong: Both halves of this were decided in pass 19 and only one shipped. UXA-4 gave this control the radiogroup role, its own comment (:580-586) arguing it "is a proper radiogroup [on the Policy sheet] — this one was simply never brought along, so the capability policy, the most consequential setting in the product, was the one a screen reader could not read." UXA-7 then wrote `app/ui/roving-radio.ts`, whose header states the rule: "A radiogroup PROMISES arrow-key navigation… Declaring the role without wiring the keys is a broken contract — the reader is told a thing works and it does not."
