corrections: Two narrowings. (1) UI-58 is a prior-pass finding ID / in-file convention comment (activity-page.tsx:313, notifications-page.tsx:247), not a binding numbered ruling in decisions.md — do not cite it as "a standing ruling". (2) The failure is degraded, not blocking: because every radio is its own tab stop, a keyboard user can still reach and set each option with Tab; what breaks is the promised interaction model (Left/Right does nothing) plus 4x the tab stops (4 modes x N capabilities). The tightest statement of the defect is the intra-product contradiction: the same `cap-seg` Direct/Recommend/Human/Off control is arrow-navigable with roving tabindex on the Policy sheet (policy-page.tsx:470-490) and is neither in the New/Edit agent profile modal (create-profile-modal.tsx:583-598), with resource-modals.tsx:342-367 ("How the skill gets its content") as the second unadopted radiogroup.

The magnitude figure is wrong. Per app/shared/capabilities.ts:61-108 an agent profile's groups are 'Repository & execution' (4 caps), 'Collaboration' (5), 'Reserved for humans' (3), and a specialist row offers 3 mode buttons, not 4 (R7-5, see create-profile-modal.tsx:509-510). So the worst real case is an expanded Collaboration group costing 15 tab stops instead of 5, not '24 instead of 6'. State it as 3-4x the tab stops (e.g. 15 instead of 5); operator profiles are the 4-mode case. Also note the secondary site at resource-modals.tsx:343-368 is a 2-option group rendered only in create mode ({!initial && ...} at :340), so its tab-stop cost is negligible — the substantive defect is the capability matrix.

confirmed.title: A server refusal inside a modal is rendered but never announced, while the success and the client-side refusal on the same button both reach the app's announcer
confirmed.what_user_sees: In org Settings → Members → Edit user, `saveAction`'s handler is `onResult: (d) => { if (!d.ok) { setErr(d.error); return; } if (d.toast) push(d.toast); onClose(); }` (:341-349; the invite modal is identical at :86-92, the reset path at :352-355). On failure the message lands in a plain `<div className="cred-warn">` (:313, :504) with no `role="alert"`, no `aria-live`, and no toast. A screen-reader user presses "Save changes", hears nothing at all, and the modal stays open looking unchanged. On success the same button pushes a toast through `app/ui/toast.tsx:216-217` (`role="status" aria-live="polite"`). The client-side refusal on the very same button — "You can't demote yourself" (:369) — also toasts. So the one branch that is silent is the server saying no. `app/features/home/new-project-modal.tsx` has the same asymmetry: success pushes a toast (:466-476) and the pre-submit blocker hint carries `role="status"` (:350), but the actual server rejection at :553-557 renders in `.form-err` with no role at all.
confirmed.why_wrong: `app/ui/toast.tsx:119-120` names itself "the app's ONE announcer" and records P16-UI-26, which existed to stop it being "silent for every dialog-driven action". The app's own convention for a submission error is a live region — `routes/login.tsx:247`, `:543` and `profile-page.tsx:169`, `:670`, `:837` all use `role="alert"`; `login.tsx:476`/`:581` even put `role="status"` on a `.cred-warn`, the identical class that carries these silent errors. R15-11 required refusals to be "rendered copy in place, not only a backgrounded toast" — that says *also* render inline, not *stop announcing*. INTENT.md §Feedback: "Errors explain what failed, what remains true, and what to do next"; an error nobody is told about explains nothing. §Accessibility requires "screen-reader announcements for consequential state changes".
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `role="alert"` to the error containers — `users-panel.tsx:313` and `:504`, `new-project-modal.tsx:554`, and the sibling `.cred-warn` error slots at `settings-page.tsx:1041`, `resource-modals.tsx:79`/`:252`/`:416`, `agent-template-modal.tsx:384`, `connections-panel.tsx:181` — matching `login.tsx:247`. Cheapest durable version: give `useOrgAction`'s failure branch the same treatment its success branch gets, or add an `err` prop to `MiniModal` that renders the one labelled, live-region error slot for all seven callers (it already owns `unmetHint` from UXA-9).
corrections: Two corrections. (1) The canon citation is wrong: R15-11 (docs/architecture/decisions.md:279-283) is about the Review queue rows naming "Review" rather than "Accept" — it says nothing about refusals. The quoted sentence comes from planning/discovery-2026-08-06-pass19/reference/UI-INVENTORY.md:163-164, a reference note that itself mis-cites R15-11. This strengthens rather than weakens the finding: no numbered ruling covers inline refusal rendering at all. corrections:
The finding is real; two details should be tightened.

NARROWER, FULLY DEFENSIBLE CLAIM
The collapsed capability-group summary in the create/edit-profile modal (`create-profile-modal.tsx:544-570`) prints unlabelled counts — e.g. a group header reading "Repository  5" or "Delivery  3  2" — where nothing in text says which mode each number counts. Because entries are conditionally rendered (`c.X > 0 &&`), position does not disambiguate either: a two-entry strip could be direct+human or recommend+off. The worst concrete case is a group whose capabilities all share one mode: it renders a single number, which reads as the group's TOTAL capability count rather than as "5 are Off". The button's accessible name is "<group> 5" with no mode word, so a screen-reader user setting the product's most consequential policy gets numbers with no referent. This is the only capability control in the modal not brought along by the pass-19 a11y work (UXA-4 at :578-586 fixed the expanded radiogroup; F19-5 at :693 fixed the resource chips).

DE-EMPHASIZE THE COLOUR-BLIND ANGLE
`--teal-dark` is `#187574` and `--coral-dark` is `#600000` (app.css:46,49) — near-black maroon vs mid teal, a large lightness gap, so "a red-green colour-blind admin cannot tell them apart" overstates it. The load-bearing defect is the absent label and the absent accessible name, not colour confusion specifically.

ONE EXTRA DRIFT WORTH FOLDING IN
The modal's fourth dot uses `.d none` (`--placeholder` #6a6e81, app.css:3821) while the product's only worded legend renders "Not granted" with `.d off` (`--ring` #e0e2e8, app.css:3820, `capability-matrix-modal.tsx:117`). So even an admin who learned the legend in the capability matrix sees a grey the legend never showed them for the same Off state.

Two sharpenings, both verified:

(1) The strongest evidence is intra-modal, not cross-page. In the SAME modal the resource accordion's collapsed header prints its summary in words — "2 of 2" (create-profile-modal.tsx:668-673, pinned by app/features/agents/agents-page.test.tsx:795) — while the capability accordion four lines earlier in the same visual family prints bare digits. One modal, two accordions, two different honesty levels.

(2) The claim understates it: the only legend that names the four dots does not even match the modal's colours. The modal's "off" swatch is `className="d none"` (create-profile-modal.tsx:565) = var(--placeholder) (#6a6e81 light / #868d9f dark), whereas capability-matrix-modal.tsx:118 and app.css:3820 use `.d.off` = var(--ring) (#e0e2e8 light / #2b2e3a dark). So an admin who opens the Capability matrix to decode the dots gets a "Not granted" swatch in a visibly different grey from the one in the editor — the decode key is wrong for one of the four states.

(3) Minor: the claim says "up to four" modes are summarised. Correct, but note that for a SPECIALIST profile the editable modes are only three — Allowed / Human-only / Off (SPECIALIST_CAP_MODES, pinned by app/features/agents/capability-catalog.test.ts:87-97, per R7-5) — while the summary still has a `recommend` branch, and the words the legend uses ("Acts directly", "Recommends", "Reserved for humans") match neither the specialist's segment labels nor Policy's ("direct/recommend/human"). Any fix should label the counts with the same words the expanded segment uses for that profile kind, not invent a fourth vocabulary.
